facts.text: Newtonville’s land was once part of the Lenape Native American territory, used for hunting and agriculture before European settlers arrived.
1700s land patents show small farms, with Dutch and Swedish farming practices blending into the English Quaker community that settled the area.
Around 125 years ago, Newtonville became a rural haven for African American families leaving Philadelphia and Camden, buying affordable farmland in the Pinelands.
Logging and blueberry farming shaped parts of Newtonville, yet much of the area remains protected by the Pinelands National Reserve.
In the early 1900s, Newtonville emerged as one of South Jersey’s 25+ historic black settlements, its land ownership shielding residents from widespread disenfranchisement.
Newtonville sits along a Conrail freight line, linking it historically to regional rail transport and the broader Atlantic County economy.
